response: Thomas Edison is famous for inventing the phonograph, which made sound records. He built it at his own factory and sold them to record companies. Then he came up with the electric version that worked on alternating current. The phone was born around 1876, about ten years after I first heard it. It changed everything, from business meetings to home calls. Nobody ever said we didn't need one.
